html:
A narrow-gauge railway, just two feet wide, that climbs about 88 kilometres from the plains of north Bengal to the hill town of Darjeeling. It was built from 1879 to 1881.

Darjeeling was a summer retreat for British officials and the centre of the Darjeeling tea estates, but the cart road up was slow. The tiny gauge let trains follow the hillside with very tight curves. To gain height the line uses loops, where the track circles over itself, and zigzags, where the train runs forward and then backward up the slope. It rises from about 100 metres above sea level to over 2,200 metres. Ghum station, near the top, was for long the highest in India.

The small steam engines, many from the 19th century, became loved as the "Toy Train". The line was one of the first hill railways of its kind, a model for others in the age after the first train in India. In 1999 it became a World Heritage Site, later joined by two other mountain railways of India.
sum: A narrow-gauge railway, just two feet wide, that climbs about 88 kilometres from the plains of north Bengal to the hill town of Darjeeling. It was built from 1879 to 1881.
